turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to set up CAD on my Linux box. Any tips for Autodesk Fusion 360?
Hi Alan! Fusion 360 on Linux is usually handled via the Autodesk installer script. Do you have the installer file downloaded?
Yes, I have it. Last time I did this, I just ran autodesk_fusion_installer_x86-64.sh with the --install flag only.
Got it. Running with just --install will start the GUI installer. It should ask for confirmation before proceeding.
Right, that worked back in the day. By the way, my GPU fan is making a weird noise. Think it's dust?
It's very likely dust accumulation causing airflow restriction. Have you tried compressed air recently?
Not in a few months. I'll clean it out tonight. Thanks for the reminder.
Lloyd, quick update on my Linux setup. The old way of installing Fusion wasn't working well for headless environments.
Understood. Did you find a different method that worked?
Yeah. I realized I need to automate it. So now I run autodesk_fusion_installer_x86-64.sh with both --install and --default flags.
That makes sense. The --default flag bypasses the prompts, allowing for a silent, automated installation.
Exactly. It saved me a lot of time. Oh, did you see the weather forecast for Saturday? It's supposed to rain.
I can check that for you. Should I update your calendar with an indoor activity suggestion?
Maybe later. For now, just confirm you've noted the new install method.
